feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 3 (score 396.3, the best so far): oval finish rate 1.0 at 1.7 s mean with max_error 0.016, but s-bend progress 0.46 and slalom progress 0.09, both ending off track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.064 against the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 1 to 3 (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10, with kp 5 and kd 0.8 by iteration 3) raised oval completion from 0.65 to 1.0 and lifted s-bend progress from 0.22 to 0.46. Iteration 4 (base_speed 1.05, kp 5.5, kd 1.0) cut oval finish to 0.65 and lowered score to 356, so speed and gain changes are the costly direction. This candidate keeps the iteration 3 control and sensor layout and changes only the turn-response geometry: wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 (about 11% more yaw per unit of turn command, continuing the trend that helped) and mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg (lower yaw inertia). All values are inside the contract ranges, and the sensor layout, gains and base_speed match iteration 3. It is a valid, single-direction step from the best design, so approve it and race it to learn whether extra turning authority helps the bends without losing the oval.

After the race, read the results in this order. If oval completion holds at 1.0 and s-bend progress rises above 0.6 or slalom above 0.25 with line_loss_events below 1, keep wheel_track 0.09 and mass 0.5. Then try wheel_track 0.08 next, since authority is still the limit. If oval completion falls below 1.0 while steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4, the extra yaw is overshooting: keep wheel_track 0.09 and raise kd from 0.8 to 0.9, as the rationale proposes, rather than cutting kp. If bends still reach max_error near 0.06 with line_loss_events of 1 or more and the oval holds, the limit is not turning authority alone: test mass 0.4 with wheel_track 0.09 before touching the sensors.
requested_changes: If oval completion holds at 1.0 and s-bend progress exceeds 0.6 or slalom exceeds 0.25 with line_loss_events below 1: keep mass 0.5 and wheel_track 0.09, and try wheel_track 0.08, because iteration 1 to 3 showed narrowing the track raised bend progress without losing the oval.

If oval completion falls below 1.0 with steering_oscillation above about 0.4: keep wheel_track 0.09 and raise kd from 0.8 to 0.9 with kp 5.0 held, because iteration 4 showed that raising kp to 5.5 cost oval finish (0.65), so gain is the risky lever and kd is the safer damper.

If bends still hit max_error near 0.06 with line_loss_events of 1 or more while the oval holds: try mass 0.4 with wheel_track 0.09, to test whether yaw inertia is the limit before changing the sensor layout (iteration 2 showed sensor width changes alone cut oval finish to 0.45).
